title: A change of target integration profile is a configuration change; the source tree does not re-shape
description: Switching the target integration from one profile to another (for example, moving a service from a Kubernetes deployment to a Docker Compose deployment behind a load balancer) is expressed as a change to the operator-declared profile name and its per-profile options. The source tree that binds the profile handlers and the profile-resolver call site do not change; the profile shift takes effect on the next process start. A source-tree change is required only when the operator authors a new custom profile or extends the shipped profile set; existing profiles are switched by configuration alone.
rationale: The elicitation surface earns its complexity by making the switch cheap. A project that pays for the resolver plus the handler-set indirection at author time must get a configuration-only migration path in return; otherwise the elicitation is theatre. A project that outgrows a profile authors a new one against the profile contract and files it under the custom slot, then changes the profile name in configuration.
